items.title: Trump cuts India tariffs to 18% after Modi pledges to halt Russian oil

featured_image.name: India gets friendship discount on Trump tariffs

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Monday that the United States and India have reached an immediate trade deal following a phone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, lowering reciprocal tariffs from 25% to 18%. Under the agreement, India committed to stop buying Russian oil and purchase over $500 billion in US energy, technology, agricultural, and other products.[1][2]

The breakthrough marks a potential turning point in bilateral relations that had grown strained over the past year, with the US imposing steep 50% tariffs on Indian exports—among the highest applied to any country—in August 2025.[3][4]

items.title: US-Iran nuclear talks planned for Friday in Istanbul

featured_image.name: Steve Witkoff is involved in Middle East, Russia-Ukraine ...

items.description:
Turkey, Qatar, and Egypt are working to arrange urgent diplomatic talks between White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with a meeting planned for Friday in Istanbul, as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran raise fears of a broader regional conflict.[1][2]

The diplomatic push comes as Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei warned Sunday that any U.S. attack would not remain limited. "The Americans should know that if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war," Khamenei said during a public address in Tehran. His comments followed the deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group to the Arabian Sea, which President Donald Trump has characterized as a "massive armada".[3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: QatarEnergy CEO says AI demand may flip LNG glut to shortage

featured_image.name: Qatar's North Field East gas expansion to begin output in mid-2026

items.description:
Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and data centers could flip the global liquefied natural gas market from projected oversupply to shortage by the end of the decade, QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned at the opening of the LNG2026 conference in Doha on Monday.

"We always thought the market would have some kind of oversupply between 2025-2030 and beyond 2030 you will have a shortage," al-Kaabi said, adding that demand expectations have increased "mainly due to AI and data center requirements, which are sustained power requirements as a baseload."[1][2][3]

The warning comes as a record wave of LNG supply begins flowing from major projects in the United States and Qatar between 2026 and 2029, which had raised concerns among analysts about a supply glut that could depress prices. Projects like Golden Pass LNG on the U.S. Gulf Coast and Qatar's North Field Expansion are expected to contribute sizable new volumes.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: SpaceX in advanced talks to merge with xAI, sources say

featured_image.name: Elon Musk's xAI Raises $20 Billion - The New York Times

items.description: Elon Musk is moving rapidly to consolidate his business empire as SpaceX and artificial intelligence firm xAI have entered advanced discussions to merge, according to Bloomberg. The companies have already informed some of their investors about the plans, with an agreement potentially coming as soon as this week.[1]

items.title: Colombia's Petro arrives in Washington for Trump summit

featured_image.name: Colombia's President, an Outspoken Trump Critic, Heads to the White House

items.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro arrived in Washington over the weekend ahead of his first face-to-face meeting with President Donald Trump, scheduled for Tuesday at the White House. The encounter aims to reset a bilateral relationship that has badly frayed over months of escalating tensions between two leaders known for their unpredictable natures.[1][2]

items.title: Pakistan says forces killed 145 militants in Balochistan

featured_image.name: Nearly 150 militants killed in 40-hour battle after deadly attacks in Pakistan

items.description:
Pakistan's security forces killed 145 militants over a 40-hour period following a wave of coordinated attacks across the southwestern province of Balochistan, marking one of the deadliest flare-ups in the region's decades-long separatist insurgency.

The violence, which erupted on Saturday across more than a dozen locations, left 17 law enforcement personnel and 31 civilians dead, according to Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, who addressed reporters in the provincial capital Quetta on Sunday.[1][2][3]

"We managed to kill 145 terrorists in 40 hours," Bugti said, describing the toll as the highest militant casualties in such a short span since Pakistan began its counterterrorism campaign. "The bodies of these 145 killed terrorists are in our custody, and some of them are Afghan nationals."[4][5][6]

items.title: Trump launches $12B critical minerals stockpile to counter China

featured_image.name: Trump plans to stockpile deep-sea metals to counter China ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump is set to launch Project Vault, a $12 billion initiative aimed at establishing a first-of-its-kind strategic critical minerals stockpile for the private sector, according to Bloomberg. The venture combines $1.67 billion in private capital with a $10 billion loan from the US Export-Import Bank to procure and store minerals for automakers, technology firms, and other manufacturers reliant on rare earths and other metals.[1][2][3]

The initiative represents the Trump administration's most aggressive effort yet to insulate American manufacturers from supply shocks and reduce reliance on Chinese-controlled supply chains. Details of the program were described by senior administration officials, though specifics about which minerals will be prioritized and where they will be stored have not been disclosed.[1]

items.title: ConocoPhillips CEO projects global LNG market to double by 2050

featured_image.name: US shale to plateau if oil stays in current range, ConocoPhillips CEO ...

items.description: Speaking at the LNG2026 conference in Doha, Qatar, ConocoPhillips Chairman and CEO Ryan Lance forecasted that the global liquefied natural gas market will double by mid-century, reaching 800 million tons from approximately 400 million tons today. The remarks underscore the energy giant's bullish outlook on natural gas as a critical fuel source for the coming decades.[1][2][3]

items.title: MIT's AI model suggests recipes for making new materials

featured_image.name: AI materials discovery now needs to move into the real world

items.description:
MIT researchers have developed an AI model called DiffSyn that can suggest promising synthesis routes for complex materials, addressing one of the most time-consuming bottlenecks in materials science. The tool, described in a paper published today in Nature Computational Science, demonstrated state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting pathways for creating zeolites, a class of materials with applications in catalysis, absorption, and ion exchange processes.[1][2]

"To use an analogy, we know what kind of cake we want to make, but right now we don't know how to bake the cake," said lead author Elton Pan, a PhD candidate in MIT's Department of Materials Science and Engineering. "Materials synthesis is currently done through domain expertise and trial and error."[2][1]

items.title: European stocks tumble as metals selloff and oil slump hit markets

featured_image.name: European shares fall as commodities-linked stocks slide - Reuters

items.description:
The pan-European Stoxx 600 declined Monday as a global selloff in precious metals and a sharp drop in oil prices sent mining and energy stocks tumbling, while investors reassessed risk assets following President Donald Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve chair.

The Stoxx 600 fell 0.4% in early trading, with the basic resources sector on track for its biggest daily decline since July 2025, dropping more than 2%. European energy stocks also slid, falling nearly 5% as oil prices tumbled on easing U.S.-Iran tensions.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: China's solar capacity to surpass coal for first time in 2026

featured_image.name: China's wind, solar power expected to reach over 500 ...

items.description:
Elon Musk is raising alarm over China's rapid energy expansion, predicting the country's electricity generation will surpass that of the United States by a factor of three within the next two years, fueled by an unprecedented solar power buildout.

"China electricity generation is still growing super fast, with solar being the largest incremental contributor, and will exceed America by a factor of 3X either this year or next," Musk wrote on X on January 31, citing a report showing China accounted for 33.2 percent of global electricity generation in 2025—more than double the US share of approximately 14.2 percent.[1][2]

items.title: India and China manufacturing expands in January amid weak confidence

featured_image.name: China's factory activity grows at fastest pace since October, private ...

items.description:
Manufacturing activity in India and China showed marginal improvement in January, with private-sector surveys indicating continued expansion even as business confidence in both nations fell to multi-year lows, highlighting persistent economic headwinds despite steady production gains.

The HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index, compiled by S&P Global, rose to 55.4 in January from December's two-year low of 55.0, according to data released Monday. In China, the RatingDog General Manufacturing PMI edged up to 50.3 from 50.1 the previous month, marking the fastest growth since October. A reading above 50 indicates expansion.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Japan retrieves rare earths from record ocean depth

featured_image.name: Japan sets sail on rare earth hunt as China tightens supplies | Reuters

items.description:
Japan announced Monday that it has successfully recovered sediment rich in rare earth elements from 6,000 meters beneath the Pacific Ocean, marking the world's first attempt to extract these critical minerals from such extreme depths. The breakthrough comes as Tokyo seeks to reduce its heavy dependence on Chinese imports amid escalating diplomatic tensions between the two nations.

The deep-sea scientific drilling vessel Chikyu collected the samples near the remote coral atoll of Minami Torishima, located roughly 1,900 kilometers southeast of Tokyo within Japan's exclusive economic zone. Government spokesperson Kei Sato described the recovery as "a meaningful achievement both in terms of economic security and comprehensive maritime development," though he noted that details would still need to be analyzed to determine the exact quantity of rare earths contained in the samples.[1][2][3]

items.title: Gold, silver extend historic sell-off as Asian markets tumble

featured_image.name: Gold, silver pull off shock move big tech never saw coming ...

items.description:
Gold and silver prices extended their sharp declines in Asian trading on Monday, deepening losses from last week's historic sell-off triggered by President Donald Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh as the next Federal Reserve chair.

Silver tumbled as much as 11.25% to $75.10 per ounce, following a nearly 30% collapse on Friday—its steepest single-day drop since 1980. Gold fell as much as 5.34% to $4,604.47 after plunging nearly 10% on Friday when it dropped below the $5,000 mark. Despite the pullback, both metals remain sharply higher year to date.[1][2][3]

items.title: Gold, platinum, palladium tumble as precious metals rout deepens

featured_image.name: CNBC Daily Open: Markets see Warsh as a safe pick for Fed chair — causing gold and silver to plunge

items.description:
Gold, platinum and palladium extended their declines on Monday, with all three metals falling more than 3% as the dramatic selloff that began late last week continued to roil precious metals markets.

The losses came as investors digested President Donald Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh to lead the Federal Reserve, a move that strengthened the dollar and prompted traders to unwind positions built during an extraordinary rally that had pushed prices to record highs.

items.title: Mexico to send Cuba humanitarian aid despite Trump pressure

featured_image.name: Mexico's Sheinbaum pledges to send humanitarian aid to Cuba ...

items.description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced Sunday that her government will send humanitarian aid to Cuba this week, including food, medicine, and basic supplies, directly contradicting President Donald Trump's claim that Mexico had complied with his request to halt oil shipments to the Caribbean island.

Speaking at an official event in the northern state of Sonora, Sheinbaum said the assistance would be coordinated by the Secretary of the Navy and aimed at alleviating shortages facing Cuban families, hospitals, and essential services. She stated emphatically that she never discussed Cuban affairs in her phone conversation with Trump on Thursday, adding that her government seeks to "diplomatically solve everything related to the oil shipments for humanitarian reasons".[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Japan's factory activity hits 3-year high as China's data diverges

featured_image.name: Japan's factory activity growth hits near 3-1/2-year peak, PMI shows

items.description:
Japan's manufacturing sector registered its strongest expansion in more than three years in January, while China's factory activity painted a mixed picture as official data showed contraction even as a private survey pointed to modest growth.

The S&P Global Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 51.5 in January from 50.0 in December, the highest reading since August 2022, according to data released Monday. The 50.0 threshold separates expansion from contraction.[1][2][3]

"Japan's manufacturing industry propelled itself back into growth territory at the start of 2026, with firms signalling the strongest upturns in output and new orders for nearly four years," said Annabel Fiddes, associate director of economics at S&P Global Market Intelligence.[4][1]

items.title: Ukraine imposes hourly power outages as harsh cold deepens energy crisis

featured_image.name: 'Normal life has disappeared': Russia's energy offensive plunges Ukraine into dark and bitter cold

items.description:
Ukraine announced that hourly power outage schedules and industrial consumption limits will take effect across all regions starting February 1-2, 2026, as the country reels from an energy crisis caused by relentless Russian attacks on its infrastructure during one of its harshest winters in recent memory.

The restrictions, announced by Ukrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned grid operator, come as temperatures in parts of the country are forecast to plunge as low as minus 30 degrees Celsius over the coming days. The schedules will apply to all categories of consumers from midnight to midnight, with residents advised to check local energy provider websites for specific outage times in their regions.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran's top diplomat says nuclear deal achievable amid US standoff

featured_image.name: Turkey's Foreign Minister Meets His Iranian Counterpart As Regional Tensions Rise

items.description:
Iran's top diplomat expressed confidence Sunday that a nuclear deal with the United States remains achievable even as both nations inch toward potential military confrontation, highlighting a volatile standoff defined by simultaneous diplomacy and displays of force.

In an interview with CNN, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he believes Tehran can reach an agreement with Washington on its nuclear program—but only if trust can be rebuilt. "Unfortunately, we have lost our trust in the US as a negotiating partner," Araghchi told the network, while noting that "fruitful" mediation by regional partners is helping advance discussions.[1][2][3]

His remarks came the same day Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei issued his sharpest warning yet to Washington, declaring that any American military strike would ignite "a regional war" across the Middle East.[4][5][6]

items.title: Israel reopens Rafah crossing as Gaza ceasefire enters new phase

featured_image.name: Trial Opening of the border crossing Between Egypt and Gaza

items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to join U.S. President Donald Trump's newly established Board of Peace continues to generate debate among international observers, as the initiative advances into its second phase of managing post-war Gaza while Netanyahu remains subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant.
